title: 1 Samuel Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 9.

questions.question: Who was the father of Saul in 1 Samuel 9?
options: Kish
Abiel
Zeror
Bechorath
questions.correctAnswer: Kish
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:1 states that Kish was the father of Saul.

questions.question: What tribe was Kish, Saul's father, from?
options: Judah
Benjamin
Ephraim
Levi
questions.correctAnswer: Benjamin
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:1 identifies Kish as a Benjamite, meaning he was from the tribe of Benjamin.

questions.question: How is Saul described in 1 Samuel 9?
options: A weak and shy young man
A choice young man, goodly, and taller than any of the people
An old man with gray hair
A skilled warrior from birth
questions.correctAnswer: A choice young man, goodly, and taller than any of the people
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:2 describes Saul as a choice young man and goodly, higher than any of the people from his shoulders upward.

questions.question: What problem did Kish face at the beginning of 1 Samuel 9?
options: He lost his oxen
He lost his asses
He was sick
He lost his sheep
questions.correctAnswer: He lost his asses
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:3 tells us that the asses of Kish were lost, prompting Saul to search for them.

questions.question: Who did Saul take with him to look for the lost asses?
options: One of his servants
His father Kish
Samuel
A neighbor
questions.correctAnswer: One of his servants
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:3 states that Kish told Saul to take one of the servants with him to seek the asses.

questions.question: Through which lands did Saul pass while searching for the asses?
options: Mount Ephraim, Shalisha, Shalim, and the land of the Benjamites
Jerusalem, Bethlehem, and Hebron
Mount Sinai and the plains of Moab
Gilead, Bashan, and Edom
questions.correctAnswer: Mount Ephraim, Shalisha, Shalim, and the land of the Benjamites
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:4 details the lands Saul passed through in search of the asses.

questions.question: What concern did Saul express when they reached the land of Zuph?
options: He worried about being attacked
He feared his father would stop caring about the asses
He wanted to return lest his father leave caring for the asses and take thought for them
He lost his servant
questions.correctAnswer: He wanted to return lest his father leave caring for the asses and take thought for them
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:5 shows Saul suggesting to return so that his father would not worry about them.

questions.question: What suggestion did Saul's servant make when Saul wanted to return?
options: To ask the people in the city for help
To visit a man of God in the city who might show them the way
To rest and continue the search the next day
To return immediately to their home
questions.correctAnswer: To visit a man of God in the city who might show them the way
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:6 states the servant suggested going to a man of God who was an honorable man and who could guide them.

questions.question: What concern did Saul have about visiting the man of God?
options: They had no gift to give him
They did not know the way
They were afraid of him
They had no food for the journey
questions.correctAnswer: They had no gift to give him
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:7 records Saul's concern about having no bread or present to bring to the man of God.

questions.question: What did Saul's servant offer to give the man of God?
options: A loaf of bread
A portion of their meat
The fourth part of a shekel of silver
A gift of oil
questions.correctAnswer: The fourth part of a shekel of silver
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:8 states the servant had the fourth part of a shekel of silver to give to the man of God.

questions.question: True or False: Beforetime in Israel, the man who inquired of God was called a Prophet.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:9 explains that beforetime the man was called a Seer, not a Prophet.

questions.question: True or False: Saul and his servant found young maidens who told them where the seer was.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:11-12 describes how young maidens going to draw water told Saul and his servant that the seer was in the city.

questions.question: True or False: The people ate the sacrifice before the seer blessed it.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:13 says the people would not eat until the seer blessed the sacrifice.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD told Samuel the day before Saul came that he would send a man from the tribe of Benjamin to anoint as captain.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:15-16 records that the LORD told Samuel the day before Saul came about sending a man from Benjamin to be captain.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 9, which action comes first?
options: Saul and his servant visit the man of God
Saul and his servant search for the lost asses
The LORD tells Samuel about Saul
Samuel invites Saul to eat with him
questions.correctAnswer: Saul and his servant search for the lost asses
questions.explanation: The search for the asses begins in 1 Samuel 9:3-4 before any other events.

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Saul and his servant do when they went up the hill to the city?
options: They asked young maidens if the seer was there
They immediately found Samuel at the gate
They searched for the lost asses
They prayed for guidance
questions.correctAnswer: They asked young maidens if the seer was there
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:11 describes how Saul and his servant found young maidens going out to draw water and asked them if the seer was there.

questions.question: According to the young maidens, why was the seer in the city that day?
options: Because there was a sacrifice of the people in the high place
Because he was searching for lost asses
Because he was visiting the king
Because he was teaching the people
questions.correctAnswer: Because there was a sacrifice of the people in the high place
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:12 states the seer was in the city because there was a sacrifice of the people that day in the high place.

questions.question: What reason did the maidens give for finding the seer before he went to eat?
options: The people would not eat until he came to bless the sacrifice
He was waiting for Saul and his servant
He was preparing the meal himself
He was teaching the people before the meal
questions.correctAnswer: The people would not eat until he came to bless the sacrifice
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:13 explains that the people would not eat until the seer came because he blessed the sacrifice first.

questions.question: What did Saul say to his servant before going to the city where the man of God was?
options: Well said; come, let us go
We must return home immediately
Let us pray before we enter
We should bring a gift for the seer
questions.correctAnswer: Well said; come, let us go
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:10 records Saul’s response to his servant’s suggestion to seek the man of God, saying, 'Well said; come, let us go.'

questions.question: What had the LORD told Samuel a day before Saul came to the city?
options: That He would send a man from Benjamin to be captain over Israel
That Saul’s family would be cursed
That the Philistines would defeat Israel
That Samuel would die soon
questions.correctAnswer: That He would send a man from Benjamin to be captain over Israel
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:15-16 shows that the LORD told Samuel He would send a man from Benjamin to anoint as captain over Israel to save His people from the Philistines.

questions.question: How did the LORD identify Saul to Samuel when Samuel saw him?
options: Behold the man whom I spake to thee of
This man will be a great prophet
He will bring peace to Israel
He is the son of a mighty man
questions.correctAnswer: Behold the man whom I spake to thee of
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:17 records the LORD telling Samuel, 'Behold the man whom I spake to thee of!' referring to Saul.

questions.question: What question did Saul ask Samuel at the gate?
options: Where is the seer's house?
Can you tell me about the lost asses?
Will you anoint me?
Where is the high place?
questions.correctAnswer: Where is the seer's house?
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:18 says Saul drew near to Samuel and asked, 'Tell me, I pray thee, where the seer's house is.'

questions.question: What did Samuel say to Saul when he asked for the seer's house?
options: I am the seer; go up before me unto the high place
You must wait until the sacrifice is finished
Come back tomorrow for answers
The seer is not here now
questions.correctAnswer: I am the seer; go up before me unto the high place
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:19 records Samuel answering, 'I am the seer: go up before me unto the high place; for ye shall eat with me to day.'

questions.question: What assurance did Samuel give Saul about his lost asses?
options: They are found; do not set your mind on them
They were taken by the Philistines
They will be found tomorrow
We will search again soon
questions.correctAnswer: They are found; do not set your mind on them
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:20 states Samuel told Saul not to worry about the asses as they were found.

questions.question: How did Saul respond to Samuel's words about his tribe and family?
options: He said he was the least of the tribes and families of Benjamin
He proudly claimed his family's greatness
He ignored Samuel's words
He questioned Samuel’s authority
questions.correctAnswer: He said he was the least of the tribes and families of Benjamin
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:21 records Saul's humility, saying he was the smallest in the tribe and his family the least of Benjamin.

questions.question: What lesson about humility can we learn from Saul's response to Samuel in verse 21?
options: True humility acknowledges one’s lowly status but accepts God’s plan
Humility means rejecting God’s promises
It is better to hide one’s identity
Pride is necessary to lead
questions.correctAnswer: True humility acknowledges one’s lowly status but accepts God’s plan
questions.explanation: Saul's acknowledgment of his humble background (1 Samuel 9:21) teaches that humility involves recognizing one’s position yet trusting God’s purpose, as Samuel had revealed (9:20).

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 9:13 promise will happen if Saul and his servant come into the city as instructed in verse 12?
options: They will find the seer before he goes to eat
They will be given a feast
They will recover the lost asses
They will meet the king
questions.correctAnswer: They will find the seer before he goes to eat
questions.explanation: Verse 13 explains that upon entering the city, Saul and his servant will find the seer before he goes to eat, connecting with the maidens' instructions in verse 12.

questions.question: How does the passage in 1 Samuel 9:15-17 teach about God's sovereignty in choosing leaders?
options: God reveals to Samuel the man He has chosen to reign over Israel
God allows the people to choose their leader by vote
Samuel chooses the leader based on appearance
Leaders are appointed by the king
questions.correctAnswer: God reveals to Samuel the man He has chosen to reign over Israel
questions.explanation: Verses 15-17 show God actively informing Samuel about the chosen leader, demonstrating divine sovereignty in leadership selection.

questions.question: True or False: The people of Israel ate the sacrifice before the seer blessed it.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:13 states that the people would not eat until the seer blessed the sacrifice, so the correct answer is False.

questions.question: True or False: Saul was described as the tallest person from his shoulders upward among the children of Israel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:2 describes Saul as being higher than any of the people from his shoulders upward, confirming the statement is True.

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 9.

questions.question: Who identified himself as the seer when Saul asked for the location of the seer's house?
options: Samuel
Kish
Saul
The servant
questions.correctAnswer: Samuel
questions.explanation: Samuel answered Saul and said, 'I am the seer,' directly identifying himself as the seer (1 Samuel 9:19).

questions.question: What reason did Samuel give Saul for not worrying about the lost asses?
options: The asses were found
They were taken by enemies
They never existed
They were sold
questions.correctAnswer: The asses were found
questions.explanation: Samuel told Saul not to set his mind on the lost asses because they were found, indicating the matter was resolved (1 Samuel 9:20).

questions.question: How did Saul describe his tribe and family when responding to Samuel's words?
options: The smallest tribe and least family
The greatest tribe and most powerful family
The oldest tribe and respected family
The richest tribe and largest family
questions.correctAnswer: The smallest tribe and least family
questions.explanation: Saul acknowledged he was from the smallest tribe of Israel, Benjamin, and that his family was the least of all families in that tribe (1 Samuel 9:21).

questions.question: Where did Samuel seat Saul during the meal with invited guests?
options: In the chiefest place among them that were bidden
At the lowest place by the door
Outside the city
Among the servants
questions.correctAnswer: In the chiefest place among them that were bidden
questions.explanation: Samuel brought Saul into the parlour and made him sit in the chiefest place among the guests, highlighting Saul's honored position (1 Samuel 9:22).

questions.question: What portion of the sacrifice was specially set aside for Saul?
options: The shoulder and that which was upon it
The head of the animal
The liver
The fat tail
questions.correctAnswer: The shoulder and that which was upon it
questions.explanation: The cook took up the shoulder and what was upon it and set it before Saul, which Samuel said had been kept for him since the invitation (1 Samuel 9:24).

questions.question: Where did Samuel and Saul converse after coming down from the high place into the city?
options: On the top of the house
In the city gate
In the temple courtyard
At the marketplace
questions.correctAnswer: On the top of the house
questions.explanation: Samuel communed with Saul on the top of the house after they came down from the high place (1 Samuel 9:25).

questions.question: What time of day did Samuel call Saul to the top of the house to send him away?
options: About the spring of the day
At sunset
At noon
At midnight
questions.correctAnswer: About the spring of the day
questions.explanation: Samuel called Saul early, about the spring of the day, indicating dawn or early morning (1 Samuel 9:26).

questions.question: What instruction did Samuel give Saul as they reached the end of the city?
options: Bid the servant pass on before us, but stand thou still a while
Follow the servant closely
Leave the servant behind and run ahead
Wait by the city gate
questions.correctAnswer: Bid the servant pass on before us, but stand thou still a while
questions.explanation: Samuel told Saul to have the servant go on ahead while he and Saul stayed back so Samuel could reveal the word of God to Saul (1 Samuel 9:27).

questions.question: What is the significance of the term 'seer' as used in this chapter?
options: It was the former title for what is now called a prophet
It was a common term for kings
It referred to priests only
It was a title for scribes
questions.correctAnswer: It was the former title for what is now called a prophet
questions.explanation: The text explains that beforetime in Israel, the one who inquired of God was called a seer, but now is called a prophet (1 Samuel 9:9).

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage foreshadows the anointing of a king like Saul, similar to the theme in 1 Samuel 9?
options: 1 Samuel 10:1
Genesis 12:1
Exodus 20:1
Psalm 23:1
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Samuel 10:1
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 10:1 records Samuel anointing Saul as king, fulfilling the foreshadowing in 1 Samuel 9:16-17 where Samuel is told to anoint the man sent by God to save Israel.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God choosing the lowly to lead, similar to Saul being from the smallest tribe?
options: 1 Corinthians 1:27
John 3:16
Romans 8:28
Hebrews 11:1
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Corinthians 1:27
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:27 speaks of God choosing the weak and lowly things to shame the strong, paralleling Saul's humble tribal background in 1 Samuel 9:21.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'seer' in this chapter?
options: Ro'eh - one who sees or beholds
Nabi - one who speaks
Cohen - priest
Melchizedek - king of righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: Ro'eh - one who sees or beholds
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for seer is 'ro'eh,' meaning one who sees or beholds, indicating a visionary role as in 1 Samuel 9:9.

questions.question: What literary device is evident in Samuel setting aside the shoulder of the sacrifice for Saul, anticipating his future role?
options: Foreshadowing
Alliteration
Hyperbole
Irony
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadowing
questions.explanation: Samuel setting aside the shoulder of the sacrifice for Saul foreshadows Saul's future importance as king, symbolically honored before the feast (1 Samuel 9:23-24).

questions.question: True or False: Samuel told Saul that the desire of Israel was not on him or his father's house.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Samuel said the desire of Israel was indeed on Saul and all his father's house (1 Samuel 9:20), so the statement is false.

questions.question: True or False: The servant suggested consulting the man of God to find the way to the lost asses.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The servant told Saul about the man of God in the city who could show them the way, suggesting they go to him (1 Samuel 9:6).

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 9:1 reveal about the nature of Saul's family background?
options: They were from a powerful and prominent family in Benjamin
They were strangers without heritage in Israel
They were priests serving in the temple
They were Philistine captives
questions.correctAnswer: They were from a powerful and prominent family in Benjamin
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 9:1 describes Kish, Saul's father, as a 'mighty man of power' from the tribe of Benjamin, indicating a family of some significance and strength within Israel.

questions.question: According to 1 Samuel 9:2, what distinguished Saul physically among the children of Israel?
options: He was taller from the shoulders upward than any other person
He had a distinctive scar on his face
He wore royal garments
He had a unique voice
questions.correctAnswer: He was taller from the shoulders upward than any other person
questions.explanation: Verse 2 clearly states that Saul was higher than any of the people from his shoulders and upward, marking him as physically notable among Israel.

questions.question: What theological implication can be drawn from God's prior revelation to Samuel about Saul in 1 Samuel 9:15-17?
options: God sovereignly chooses leaders to fulfill His redemptive plan
God rejects all from the tribe of Benjamin
God desires Saul to remain a private citizen
God postpones leadership until Saul’s descendants
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly chooses leaders to fulfill His redemptive plan
questions.explanation: Verses 15-17 show God telling Samuel in advance about Saul’s coming and his anointing as captain, demonstrating divine sovereignty in appointing leaders for His purposes (cf. Romans 13:1).

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 9:6-7 illustrate human dependence on divine guidance amidst uncertainty?
options: Saul’s servant suggests seeking a man of God to find direction
Saul confidently finds the asses without help
Saul ignores divine aid and relies on his own wisdom
Saul offers sacrifices to the Philistines for guidance
questions.correctAnswer: Saul’s servant suggests seeking a man of God to find direction
questions.explanation: In verses 6-7, the servant encourages Saul to consult a man of God, showing recognition that human wisdom is insufficient without divine direction.

questions.question: What does the term 'seer' in 1 Samuel 9:9 reveal about prophetic ministry in Israel's history?
options: The prophetic office was previously known as 'seer', emphasizing divine revelation
Seers were unrelated to prophets and only predicted weather
The term 'seer' was a derogatory name for false prophets
Prophets were only kings and priests, not seers
questions.correctAnswer: The prophetic office was previously known as 'seer', emphasizing divine revelation
questions.explanation: Verse 9 explains that 'seer' was the earlier term for one who inquired of God, highlighting the continuity and divine source of prophetic revelation.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God’s providence is taught by 1 Samuel 9:20 where Samuel tells Saul not to worry about the lost asses?
options: God’s providence cares for even small details while focusing on His greater purposes
God is indifferent to human concerns
God punishes Saul for losing the asses
God only cares about the animals, not people
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providence cares for even small details while focusing on His greater purposes
questions.explanation: Samuel’s reassurance in verse 20 shows that God has already resolved the lost asses’ issue, reflecting His providential care over both minor and major concerns (cf. Matthew 6:26).

questions.question: How does the narrative of Saul’s search for his father’s asses in 1 Samuel 9:3-5 typify human need for God’s direction in life’s pursuits?
options: It symbolizes the seeking of God’s guidance when facing lost or uncertain situations
It illustrates Saul’s independence from divine help
It shows that material possessions are more important than spiritual things
It indicates that Saul was negligent in his duties
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the seeking of God’s guidance when facing lost or uncertain situations
questions.explanation: The search for lost asses represents broader human experiences of confusion and the need for divine direction, as Saul ultimately seeks the seer’s guidance (verses 3-5).

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted by the fact that all Samuel’s prophetic words come true, as mentioned in 1 Samuel 9:6?
options: God’s faithfulness and truthfulness in fulfilling His promises
God’s wrath against disobedient nations
God’s hiddenness and silence
God’s anger toward Saul
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness and truthfulness in fulfilling His promises
questions.explanation: Verse 6 states that all Samuel says surely comes to pass, demonstrating God’s attribute of faithfulness and truthfulness (Numbers 23:19).

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 9:13-14 contribute to the theological understanding of priestly blessing in Israel’s worship system?
options: The people waited for the seer to bless the sacrifice before eating, showing the mediator role of God’s servants
The people ate before any blessing was pronounced
The seer refused to bless sacrifices
Sacrifices were offered without any human involvement
questions.correctAnswer: The people waited for the seer to bless the sacrifice before eating, showing the mediator role of God’s servants
questions.explanation: Verses 13-14 show that the seer’s blessing was essential before the people ate, illustrating the priestly function of mediating God’s favor in worship.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight do 1 Samuel 9:21 and 1 Samuel 9:17 provide about God's choice of leaders?
options: God chooses leaders not by human status but by divine purpose and calling
Only the most prominent families are chosen by God
Leaders must be physically the tallest to be chosen
God rejects those who doubt their worth
questions.correctAnswer: God chooses leaders not by human status but by divine purpose and calling
questions.explanation: In verse 21, Saul expresses his low status, but verse 17 shows God affirming Saul as the chosen king, teaching that God's election transcends human social standing (cf. 1 Corinthians 1:27).

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 9:22-24 illustrate the principle of God’s providential preparation for His purposes?
options: Samuel had set aside a portion of food specifically for Saul in anticipation of his arrival
Samuel was unaware of Saul’s coming and made no preparation
Saul was excluded from the meal with invited guests
The people rejected Saul’s presence at the feast
questions.correctAnswer: Samuel had set aside a portion of food specifically for Saul in anticipation of his arrival
questions.explanation: Verses 22-24 show Samuel instructing the cook to set aside a portion for Saul, indicating God's providential orchestration of events to welcome Saul.

questions.question: What does 1 Samuel 9:19 teach about the identity and role of the prophet in Israel?
options: The prophet is the seer who reveals God’s word and shares fellowship with God’s people
The prophet is a political leader only
The prophet is a silent figure with no public role
The prophet acts independently of God’s instruction
questions.correctAnswer: The prophet is the seer who reveals God’s word and shares fellowship with God’s people
questions.explanation: Verse 19 has Samuel declaring himself the seer and inviting Saul to eat with him, highlighting the prophet’s role as God’s spokesman and community leader.

questions.question: What combined theological teaching do 1 Samuel 9:16 and 1 Samuel 9:27 convey about God’s revelation and human response?
options: God reveals His plans to His prophets and calls individuals to patiently wait for His word
God hides His plans and expects immediate human action
God’s revelation is only for kings, not prophets
Human initiative alone can replace divine revelation
questions.correctAnswer: God reveals His plans to His prophets and calls individuals to patiently wait for His word
questions.explanation: Verse 16 shows God revealing His plan to Samuel, and verse 27 depicts Samuel asking Saul to wait for God’s word, teaching the necessity of divine revelation and patient human response.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that biblical narratives like Saul searching for lost asses (1 Samuel 9:3-5) are trivial and irrelevant to understanding God’s plan. What does 1 Samuel 9:3-6 actually teach about God’s providential involvement in human affairs?
options: Even seemingly minor events lead to divine appointments and reveal God’s guidance
The narrative is purely historical with no theological meaning
Saul’s search is a metaphor for human futility without God
God is indifferent to daily human problems
questions.correctAnswer: Even seemingly minor events lead to divine appointments and reveal God’s guidance
questions.explanation: Verses 3-6 demonstrate how a simple search for lost animals leads Saul to the seer, showing God’s providential hand in directing human lives toward His redemptive purposes (cf. Proverbs 16:9).

questions.question: What broader redemptive theme is underscored by Saul’s anointing as captain over Israel in 1 Samuel 9:16-17 in the context of Israel’s deliverance from the Philistines?
options: God raises chosen leaders to deliver His people, prefiguring Christ the ultimate deliverer
Only military strength is needed for salvation
Israel is abandoned to its enemies without hope
Saul’s kingship is unrelated to God’s salvation plan
questions.correctAnswer: God raises chosen leaders to deliver His people, prefiguring Christ the ultimate deliverer
questions.explanation: Verses 16-17 reveal God’s intention for Saul to save Israel from Philistine oppression, foreshadowing the Messiah’s ultimate deliverance (cf. Luke 1:68-69).
